measures.title: Online Sports Wagering Authorization (constitutional amendment)
measures.summary: This citizen initiative would amend the Nebraska Constitution to allow laws letting people located in Nebraska place sports bets through an online platform. Online betting could be offered only by an authorized gaming operator that runs games of chance at a licensed racetrack in Nebraska. It is paired with Initiative 441, which would write the rules for online sports wagering into state law.
measures.yesMeans: You vote FOR amending the constitution to authorize laws allowing online sports wagering offered by licensed racetrack gaming operators.
measures.noMeans: You vote AGAINST, and the constitution is not amended in this manner.

measures.title: Online Sports Wagering Regulation (statute)
measures.summary: This citizen initiative would change state law to let people located in Nebraska place sports bets through an online platform offered by an authorized gaming operator at a licensed racetrack, or by that operator's platform provider. It would amend the Nebraska Racetrack Gaming Act to regulate such online wagering and would become operative on January 1, 2027.
measures.yesMeans: You vote FOR enacting statutes that allow and regulate online sports wagering through licensed racetrack gaming operators or their platform providers.
measures.noMeans: You vote AGAINST, and no such statutes are enacted.

measures.title: Fairness for Girls (constitutional amendment)
measures.summary: This citizen initiative would amend the Nebraska Constitution to require schools to designate each athletic team or sport as male, female, or coed/mixed based on biological sex, and to bar students of the male sex from teams designated for females. It would apply to public schools, public colleges and universities, and private schools or institutions whose teams compete against them.
measures.yesMeans: You vote FOR adding sex-based designation of school sports teams to the constitution, with female teams closed to students of the male sex.
measures.noMeans: You vote AGAINST, and the constitution is not amended in this manner.

measures.title: A constitutional amendment to change the limit on legislative terms from two consecutive terms to three consecutive terms
measures.summary: Placed on the ballot by the Nebraska Legislature, this amendment would let state senators serve three consecutive four-year terms instead of two before having to sit out for four years. Service of more than half a term would still count as a full term.
measures.yesMeans: You vote FOR allowing state senators to serve up to three consecutive terms.
measures.noMeans: You vote AGAINST, and the limit stays at two consecutive terms.
